headline: Nearly 7 lakh fail as SSC pass rate hits 19-year low
summary: Educationists point to systemic failure as girls outperform boys for the 11th consecutive year.
details: The Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and equivalent examination results have been released, revealing a significant decline in performance.
Nearly 700,000 students failed to pass the exams, marking the lowest pass rate in 19 years.
Educationists have expressed concern, attributing the sharp drop in results to a failure within the education system.
Despite the overall decline, girls have continued to lead the results, outperforming boys for the 11th year in a row.
The results have sparked a debate among experts regarding the quality of education and the need for systemic reforms to prevent further decline in student performance.

headline: Tk 1.21 crore robbed from Uttara fuel pump official
summary: Armed assailants intercepted a cash-carrying vehicle and hacked an assistant manager before fleeing with the money.
details: Armed assailants intercepted a cash-carrying vehicle in Dhaka’s airport area yesterday morning, robbing Tk 1.21 crore from a filling station official.
The victim, Mohammad Al Amin, 49, assistant manager of DL Filling Station in Uttara, was transporting the cash to a Pubali Bank branch in a covered van.
Six to seven armed men on three motorcycles intercepted the vehicle in front of Crowne Plaza on the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway around 10:30 am.
When Al Amin refused to hand over the money, one assailant held a pistol to his chest while another hacked him with a machete, injuring his elbow, palm, and leg.
The attackers snatched the khaki-coloured bag containing the money and fled towards Abdullahpur on motorcycles.
Al Amin received treatment at Kuwait Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital following the attack.
The manager of the filling station, Md Abdul Karim, stated that depositing cash to the bank five days a week is part of their regular operation.
Police, Rab and the Detective Branch have launched a coordinated investigation and are reviewing CCTV footage to identify and arrest the suspects.
caption:
Tk 1.21 crore stolen in a daring daylight robbery in Uttara. An official was hacked and threatened with a pistol to secure the cash.

The victim, Mohammad Al Amin, 49, assistant manager of DL Filling Station in Uttara, was transporting the cash to a Pubali Bank branch in a covered van.

Six to seven armed men on three motorcycles intercepted the vehicle in front of Crowne Plaza on the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway around 10:30 am.

When Al Amin refused to hand over the money, one assailant held a pistol to his chest while another hacked him with a machete, injuring his elbow, palm, and leg.

The attackers snatched the khaki-coloured bag containing the money and fled towards Abdullahpur on motorcycles.

Al Amin received treatment at Kuwait Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital following the attack.

The manager of the filling station, Md Abdul Karim, stated that depositing cash to the bank five days a week is part of their regular operation.

Police, Rab and the Detective Branch have launched a coordinated investigation and are reviewing CCTV footage to identify and arrest the suspects.
